case.case_title: Wickramasinghe v. Edmund Jayasinghe, Secretary, Ministry of Media, Tourism and Aviation

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was discriminated against on prohibited grounds under Article 12(2) by the differential application of censorship regulations.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the relaxation of censorship for state-controlled and foreign media, but not for his newspaper, constituted discrimination violating Article 12(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondent argued that the Competent Authority's discretionary power to regulate all media negates any claim of discrimination, and that the regulations are justified by national security concerns.
key_facts: The petitioner alleges favored treatment to some media allowed to self-regulate censorship.
The Competent Authority retains discretionary power to act against any media including the petitioner.
The regulations were imposed during a national emergency and civil war.
The petitioner ceased publication of military-related news due to the regulations.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that differential treatment in the application of the regulations does not amount to discrimination under Article 12(2) if the power to regulate remains with the Competent Authority and is exercised based on necessity. The Court emphasized the context of national security and the ongoing civil war as justifying the regulations.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found no evidence that the petitioner was discriminated against on any prohibited ground under Article 12(2). The alleged favored treatment to some media was not absolute and the Competent Authority could intervene if necessary. The petitioner’s refusal to comply with censorship did not establish discrimination.
principles_established: Discretionary regulatory power that applies to all media negates claims of discrimination under Article 12(2).
Context of national security can justify differential treatment without violating anti-discrimination provisions.
precedents_cited: Joseph Perera v. The Attorney General

outcome.holding: The Court refused leave to proceed on the basis that no prima facie case of discrimination under Article 12(2) was made out.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was directly engaged by the petitioner's claim of discrimination in the application of censorship regulations. The Court’s reasoning and outcome depended on interpreting whether differential treatment constituted prohibited discrimination.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court held that differential treatment of media does not per se constitute discrimination under Article 12(2) as the Competent Authority retains discretionary power to act against any media; no prima facie discrimination was shown.
